study.x: Market complementarity between potential liner-shipping alliance partners
study.time_horizon: Formation of the proposed vessel-sharing alliance

x_contrast.higher: More nonoverlapping markets, retaining at least one common market

study.setting: Two liner-shipping firms consider forming a vessel-sharing alliance. Both must participate voluntarily. They share at least one market. Market complementarity concerns nonoverlapping market coverage and is distinct from compatibility of operating resources.
study.task: Rate how higher market complementarity changes the likelihood that the firms establish a vessel-sharing alliance. Compare lower X (More overlapping market portfolios) with higher X (More nonoverlapping markets, retaining at least one common market). Use the same X contrast in both contexts. A positive rating means higher X is associated with more Y; a negative rating means less Y. Rate the relationship, not the overall level of Y. Do not interpret this judgment as a measured empirical coefficient.
shared_facts: The outcome is whether the potential vessel-sharing alliance forms, not the performance of an established alliance.
The lower-versus-higher market-complementarity contrast retains at least one common market and is identical across contexts.

source_evidence.citation: Mitsuhashi, H., and Greve, H. R. (2009). A Matching Theory of Alliance Formation and Organizational Success: Complementarity and Compatibility. Academy of Management Journal, 52(5), 975-995.
source_evidence.measurementNotes: Global liner shipping; market definitions and resource compatibility held constant
source_evidence.translationNotes: Index is symmetric difference divided by union, but zero when no common market. Economic values are unweighted. Matching requires mutual participation.

attribute_definitions.information_access: Which substantive information is available, when it is available, or who can observe it; distinguish from accuracy.
attribute_definitions.information_dependence: Shared sources, overlapping signals or correlated errors, holding marginal accuracy distinct.
attribute_definitions.interpretation_compatibility: Common vocabulary, data formats, interpretive constraints or ability to reconcile the same evidence.
attribute_definitions.verification_process: Cost, effort or procedure of checking evidence or actions; preserve any fixed verification level.
attribute_definitions.feedback_timing: When consequences or diagnostic feedback become observable, rather than how often X changes.
attribute_definitions.coordination_constraints: Compatibility, synchronized choices, matching requirements or reciprocal adjustment dependence.
attribute_definitions.adjustment_scope: The number or allocation of tasks/parties that must revise operations, distinct from compatibility itself.
attribute_definitions.work_distribution: How a fixed total burden is distributed across parties.
attribute_definitions.choice_defaults: Initialization, defaults or established conventions with choice rights held explicit.
attribute_definitions.implementation_latency: Time between an available decision and its implementation or certification.
attribute_definitions.decision_windows: Deadlines, decision frequency, meeting calendars or available time for adjustment.
attribute_definitions.reversibility: Recoverability or restoration expense after a commitment, distinct from detecting its consequences.
attribute_definitions.transition_continuity: Whether incumbent operations can continue during replacement, qualification or transition.
attribute_definitions.exit_cost: Losses or costs associated with leaving an arrangement, distinct from temporary interruption.
attribute_definitions.resource_slack: Spare capacity, buffers, staffing or resource availability.
attribute_definitions.incentive_alignment: Compatibility of interests, compensation opportunities or distributive preferences.
attribute_definitions.authority_allocation: Who can decide, veto or authorize an action; preserve fixed governance definitions.
attribute_definitions.knowledge_continuity: Retention or transfer of role-specific experience through handovers, records or briefing.
attribute_definitions.routine_reuse: Recurrence that permits procedures or administrative routines to be reused.
attribute_definitions.communication_access: Communication channels, meeting access or communication costs.
attribute_definitions.enforcement_reach: Who can apply consequences once a violation is established, distinct from detecting it.
attribute_definitions.enforcement_latency: Delay in obtaining a remedy after evidence exists.
attribute_definitions.external_approval: Outside authorization requirements or approval procedures.
attribute_definitions.experimentation_cost: Cost, scale or opportunity to trial an option before commitment.
attribute_definitions.disruption_stakes: Consequences of interruption or mismatch, distinct from its likelihood.
